# Conventions

Working agreements for this repository.

## Generated Files — Do Not Edit

The following files are generated by tooling and must never be edited by hand:

- `src/routeTree.gen.ts` — generated by TanStack Router (auto-updates on route file changes)
- `src/web/graphql/generated.ts` — generated by `npm run graphql:generate` (client types, `GqlC*` prefix)
- `src/server/graphql/generated.ts` — generated by `npm run graphql:generate` (server types, `GqlS*` prefix)
- `drizzle/` — generated by `npm run db:generate` (migration files)

To regenerate GraphQL types after a schema change:

```bash
npm run graphql:generate
```

## Database Schema (Drizzle)

### Adding a new table

1. Define the table in `src/server/db/schema.ts` using `pgTable()`
2. Export the inferred types: `type Foo = typeof foo.$inferSelect` and `type FooCreate = typeof foo.$inferInsert`
3. Generate a migration: `npm run db:generate`
4. Apply the migration: `npm run db:migrate`
5. For quick iteration during development, `npm run db:push` pushes schema changes directly without generating a migration file

### Using row types outside `schema.ts`

Always import the exported aliases (`Foo`, `FooCreate`) — never write `typeof foo.$inferSelect` / `typeof foo.$inferInsert` outside
`schema.ts`. Those helpers exist only to define the aliases.

```ts
// Good
import type { GiftCard, GiftCardCreate } from '../db/schema';

async function insertGiftCard(overrides: Partial<GiftCardCreate> = {}): Promise<GiftCard> { … }

// Bad — duplicates the alias already exported from schema.ts
async function insertGiftCard(
    overrides: Partial<typeof giftCards.$inferInsert> = {},
): Promise<typeof giftCards.$inferSelect> { … }
```

### Adding a column to an existing table

Same workflow as above — modify the table definition in `schema.ts`, then generate and apply the migration.

### Entity ids (nanoId)

Persisted primary keys and foreign keys are **20-character nanoIds** (URL-safe alphabet, compact in APIs and logs), declared via the
`nanoId()` helper in `src/server/db/schema.ts` (`varchar(20)`). Create new ids with `idCreate()` from `src/shared/idCreate.ts`. Zod
validators use `zNanoId` from the same module. **Do not** use `crypto.randomUUID()` for entity ids. That shared module is imported by web
code — keep it free of Node builtins (`node:crypto`, etc.). Test-only helpers such as `phoneNumberCreate` live in
`src/server/test/phoneNumberCreate.ts`.

### Phone numbers

Persist `Users.phoneNumber` as **E.164 with a leading `+` and country code** (e.g. `+4915123456789`). Use `phoneNumberAssert` /
`phoneNumberNormalize` from `src/shared/phoneNumber.ts` on every write path. Reject local trunk numbers (`0152…`) — they have no country
code. WhatsApp / Meta sends use the same normalize, then `phoneNumberForWhatsAppApi` (digits only, no `+`).

### Text / email / title normalization

Commands own normalization on every write path (GraphQL scalars are format gates only). Helpers live in `src/shared/`:

| Helper                                            | Use for                                                                                             |
| ------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `emailNormalize`                                  | Persist / uniqueness for all email columns (`trim` + lowercase)                                     |
| `textNormalizeSingleLine`                         | Short fields that should not keep internal double spaces                                            |
| `textNormalizeTitled`                             | Names, titles, occasions, subjects, preference chips (`singleLine` + capitalize first letter)       |
| `textNormalizeTitledOrNull`                       | Optional titled fields (`null` when blank)                                                          |
| `textNormalizeProse` / `textNormalizeProseTitled` | Multiline copy (biography, descriptions, messages); collapses horizontal whitespace, keeps newlines |
| `invoiceAddressNormalize`                         | Invoice JSON (`firstName` / `lastName` / `companyName` / address lines)                             |

Do **not** force Title Case of every word (preserves `McDonald`, particles, intentional internal caps). UI may apply the same helpers for
feedback; never rely on the client alone.

### Column vocabulary and JSONB shapes

`schema.ts` should stay tables + `$inferSelect` / `$inferInsert` row aliases. Hand-written unions and structured payloads used by `$type<>`
on `varchar` / `jsonb` columns live under `src/server/domain/` (entity-named modules such as `giftCard.ts`, `outboundEmail.ts`,
`chatMessage.ts`). `schema.ts` imports those types; it does not define them inline.

Chat assistant JSONB payloads that already live in `src/server/db/chatPayloadTypes.ts` stay there until moved — same rule applies to new
shapes: prefer `domain/` over growing `schema.ts`.

**Web must not import from `src/server/db/` or `src/server/domain/`.** Client code uses generated GraphQL types (`GqlC*`) only. Enforced by
ESLint `no-restricted-imports` on `src/web/**`.

### Bilingual columns

For text that ships in DE and EN (editable content-model records), the convention is **paired `*De` / `*En` text columns** rather than a
JSONB `{ de, en }` blob:

- `roleDe varchar`, `roleEn varchar` — both required if the field is required
- `subjectDe varchar default ''`, `subjectEn varchar default ''` — both default if the field is optional

The GraphQL schema mirrors the same pair as `roleDe: String!`, `roleEn: String!`. The client renders the locale-matching half, same as the
inline `{ de, en }[locale]` copy pattern used in routes. JSONB for two-key bilingual data is Postgres-native overhead; the column-pair shape
keeps `WHERE roleDe ILIKE …` queries trivial. See [`docs/architecture/content-model.md`](./architecture/content-model.md). One-language
values (a chat title, a log line) stay a single column.

## Icons

Use [Lucide React](https://lucide.dev/icons/) for all icons. It is already installed as `lucide-react`.

Always import the **Icon-suffixed** variant. This is enforced by ESLint (`no-restricted-imports`).

```tsx
// Good
import { ChevronRightIcon } from 'lucide-react';

// Bad — will fail lint
import { ChevronRight } from 'lucide-react';
```

## Naming Strategy

This project uses **entity-action naming** where file and function names lead with the entity (or domain concept) followed by the action or
role:

| Category  | Pattern                                                  | Examples                                             |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| Commands  | `{entity}{Action}`                                       | `sessionUpsert`, `userCreate`                        |
| Queries   | `{accessPath}{Entity}{FindOne\|FindMany\|Count\|Counts}` | `userFindOne`, `sessionFindMany`, `publicFooFindOne` |
| Mappers   | `toGql{Entity}`                                          | `toGqlSession`, `toGqlUser`                          |
| Guards    | `guard{Entity}{Ctx}`                                     | `guardUserSubscription`, `guardUserMutation`         |
| Factories | `{entity}Create`                                         | `serverRuntimeCreate`, `resolversCreate`             |
| Utils     | `{entity}Utils`                                          | `sessionUtils`                                       |
| Emails    | `{Sender}For{Audience}Email`                             | see [Email template naming](#email-template-naming)  |
| Tests     | `{source}.test`                                          | `sessionUtils.test`, `sessionUpsert.test`            |
| Types     | `PascalCase`                                             | `ServerRuntime`, `PubSubPostgres`                    |
| Pages     | see [Page component naming](#page-component-naming)      | `AdminUsersPage`, `ProfileCookMealPage`              |

This keeps related files sorted together in directory listings (all `session`\* files appear next to each other).

### Email template naming

Transactional React Email templates under `src/server/email/templates/` use **`{Sender}For{Audience}Email`**:

- **`Sender`** — PascalCase of the module that calls `email.send`: a command (`giftCardPay` → `GiftCardPay`), a job
  (`bookingRequestOfferCallSlotReminder` → `BookingRequestOfferCallSlotReminder`), or a dedicated send util (`bookingRequestCooksNotify` →
  `BookingRequestCooksNotify`). Not the domain event and not the `OutboundEmailPurpose` value.
- **`Audience`** — `User` (role-agnostic account/auth), `Customer`, `Cook`, or `Admin`.
- **Exports** — component `FooForBarEmail`, subject helper `fooForBarEmailSubject`, file `templates/FooForBarEmail.tsx`. Preview files under
  `email/previews/{domain}/` use short `{action}-for-{audience}.{locale}.tsx` names (folder already carries domain context; React Email
  sidebar shows the raw filename).
- **One audience per sendable file.** When one sender fans out to two roles, use two template files (shared markup may live under
  `email/components/` when the body is identical). Non-audience variants (e.g. testimonial `kind`) stay as props.
- **Out of scope** — shared shell components (`EmailLayout`, `EmailHeader`, …) and `emailStyles.ts` live under `email/components/` and keep
  the `Email*` prefix where they are components.
- **`OutboundEmailPurpose`** — persisted SCREAMING_SNAKE classifiers on `OutboundEmails`; existing values are stable and need not mirror the
  template filename. See [styles/emails.md](./styles/emails.md).

### Page component naming

Page modules live under `src/web/pages/` (mirroring the route tree). File name, exported component, colocated `.graphql` operation name, and
related camelCase helpers (`*PageTitle`, `*PageVariables`, generated `GqlC*PageQuery`) all share the same stem.

**Singular / plural** encodes cardinality — not a `Detail` / `List` suffix:

| Role                         | Pattern                      | Examples                                         |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| Collection list              | plural entity                | `AdminUsersPage`, `CitiesPage`                   |
| Single-entity read           | singular entity              | `AdminUserPage`, `CityPage`                      |
| Collection dashboard         | plural + `Overview`          | `AdminUsersOverviewPage`                         |
| Create / edit action surface | singular + `Create` / `Edit` | `AdminUserCreatePage`, `ProfileCookMealEditPage` |

Do **not** use `DetailPage` or `ListPage`. Prefer the singular/plural split already used by public pages (`BlogPostsPage` / `BlogPostPage`)
and content-model admin pages (`AdminCitiesPage` / `AdminCityPage`).

**Shell prefixes** mark which chrome owns the page:

| Shell    | Prefix            | Examples                                                                       |
| -------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Admin    | `Admin`           | `AdminUsersPage`, `AdminUserPage`                                              |
| Cook     | `ProfileCook`     | `ProfileCookMealsPage`, `ProfileCookBookingRequestOfferPage`                   |
| Customer | `ProfileCustomer` | `ProfileCustomerBookingRequestsPage`, `ProfileCustomerBookingRequestOfferPage` |

Shared surfaces that are not cook- or customer-specific stay unprefixed beyond the shell (`AccountPage`, `ProfileLayout`, `ProfilePage`).
Cook/customer overview bodies are `ProfilePageCook` / `ProfilePageCustomer` (rendered by `ProfilePage`).

Word order after the prefix is **owner → entity → role**: e.g. `ProfileCustomerBookingRequestOfferPage` (customer viewing an offer), not
`ProfileBookingRequestCustomerOfferPage`.

### Query naming

**Prefer `FindOne` / `FindMany` (and `Count` / `Counts`) for every new resolver-mounted query.** Do not mass-rename existing helpers that
already use another verb — apply the suffix convention on net-new work and when a file is already being touched for a related change.

`{accessPath}{Entity}{Suffix}` is the pattern for every file under `src/server/queries/` and for Query-side field names in
`schema.graphqls`.

**`src/server/queries/` only holds functions that are wired directly into a resolver** (imported from `resolversCreate.ts`). Shared read
helpers that are not resolver-mounted — filter builders (`*CriterionWhere`), batch loaders / hydrators (`*Hydrate`), published-row lookups,
HTTP-route loaders — live outside `queries/` (typically `src/server/utils/` or `src/server/db/`). **One resolver-mounted query function per
file** — do not colocate `FindMany` and `FindOne` (or a private hydrate helper) in the same module.

- **`accessPath`** — the GraphQL namespace the query is mounted under (e.g. `public`, `session`). **When you add an admin GraphQL
  namespace** (`User.admin` / `Mutation.admin`, see [architecture/authorization-admin.md](./architecture/authorization-admin.md)), mount
  those queries under the `admin` access path (`adminThingFindOne`, `adminThingFindMany`, …) and keep domain-owned GraphQL types / inputs /
  commands on the same access-path prefix. Free-floating (prefix-less) type names stay reserved for entities genuinely shared across access
  paths (`User`, `Session`, `Chat`, `FileUpload`, …).
- **`Entity`** — the entity (or entity-with-sub-namespace) being read.
- **`Suffix`** — return cardinality: `FindOne` (one row / singleton namespace), `FindMany` (array), `Counts` (parallel integers — one per
  input criterion, same order). Admin list totals use `Counts(criteria: [Criterion!]!): [Int!]!` (list pages pass a single criterion;
  overviews pass several for facet cards). Empty criteria are rejected; cap length (e.g. 20) so clients cannot fan out unbounded queries.
  Pagination / sort fields on the criterion bag are ignored for counts. Do not add singular `Count(criterion): Int!` fields on `Admin`.

Filters that narrow a `FindMany` stay as arguments on the same function (or a shared `*CriterionWhere` helper under `utils/`). Do not coin a
new query file for every filter axis.

### Type & input naming — the entity access path

Object types, inputs, enums, and DB tables that belong to **one GraphQL namespace** carry that namespace's access-path prefix (`Admin…` when
using the admin namespace). A free-floating (prefix-less) name is reserved for types **genuinely shared across access paths** (`User`,
`Session`, `Chat`, `FileUpload`, `MutationResult`, `Log`, `GeoCoordinates`, …).

| Layer                     | Pattern                                   | Example                                          |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| GraphQL object / input    | `{AccessPath}{Entity}` / `…Input`         | `AdminThing`, `AdminThingInput`                  |
| DB table (`pgTable('…')`) | same physical name as the GraphQL type    | `pgTable('AdminThing', …)`                       |
| Drizzle export const      | plain camelCase plural (**not** prefixed) | `export const things = pgTable('AdminThing', …)` |
| Mutation + `commands/`    | `{accessPath}{Entities}{Action}`          | `adminThingsUpsert`                              |
| Query + `queries/`        | `{accessPath}{Entity}{Suffix}`            | `adminThingFindMany`                             |

**Action inputs omit a trailing `Input`.** Mutation payloads named for a verb (`Create`, `Update`, `Upsert`, `Pay`, …) follow
`{AccessPath?}{Entity}{Action}` — `UserCreate`, `GiftCardPay`, `AdminBookingRequestOfferUpdate`, `CityUpsert`. Reserve the `…Input` suffix
for **shape / value** inputs that are not themselves an action (`GeoCoordinatesInput`, `InvoiceAddressInput`, `CookMenuCourseInput`,
`ContentSectionInput`). When an output object and matching input share a shape, pair them as `GeoCoordinates` + `GeoCoordinatesInput`
(GraphQL forbids one name across object and input kinds).

LLM-facing agent tool names stay short and prefix-less (`thingsUpsert`) — they are a sub-agent's private vocabulary. The GraphQL mutations
and `commands/` they call keep the access-path form.

Physical table renames are hand-authored `ALTER TABLE … RENAME` migrations — Drizzle's differ cannot tell a rename from a drop+create.

## Bilingual Copy

The site ships in DE and EN with no i18n library. Prefer the inline `{ de: '…', en: '…' }[locale]` literal **at the call site** in JSX:

```tsx
<h1>{{ de: 'Über uns', en: 'About us' }[locale]}</h1>
```

Colocating the strings with the elements that render them keeps context obvious, makes dead-code removal automatic, and avoids the naming
tax of a centralised `COPY` object. Do **not** hoist a page-level `COPY` const.

Hoist a string to a small local `const` only when one of the following narrow exceptions applies:

- **Reused inside the same file.** A title that appears in both `seoMeta()` inside `head()` and an `<h1>` inside the component is the
  canonical case. Give it a descriptive name (`title`, `intro`, `closeLabel`) — one const per string, not a god-object.
- **Needed outside JSX.** `seoMeta()` titles/descriptions, `aria-label`, `title`, `alt`, JSON-LD answers, anything passed to a non-JSX API.
- **Long enough to drown out the JSX.** A multi-line marketing paragraph may read better as a named const above the `return`. A single
  sentence stays inline.

**Caller-facing string props are mandatory.** Shared components that accept user-visible copy (`DatePicker` / `DateField` `placeholder`,
`MessageComposer` `ariaLabel` / `placeholder`, etc.) must require those props — never default to an English-only string. Callers pass
`{ de, en }[locale]` at the call site so TypeScript catches omissions. Universal chrome inside base / chat primitives (`Dialog` / `Sheet`
close, `Spinner` loading, pagination labels, breadcrumb landmark / ellipsis, message-scroller jump buttons, `MessageComposer` Send / Attach
/ disclaimer, chat transcript messages region) may localize via `useLocale()` inside the primitive so every surface inherits it.

**Both sides of every pair must be real locale copy.** Identical `de` / `en` is fine when the word is the same in both languages (`Name`,
`Status`, brand names). It is **not** fine when German has a clear equivalent — write `Fähigkeiten` not `Skills`, `Protokolle` not `Logs`.
Prefer translating UI chrome even when the English loanword is common in German tech speech.

**No mid-sentence em or en dashes (`—` / `–`) in user-facing copy.** They read as AI-generated. Prefer commas, periods, colons, or
parentheses. Empty-value placeholders that render a lone `—` for missing data are fine, as are en dashes in numeric or alphabetic ranges
(`12:00–13:00`, `A–Z`). Document/comment prose is out of scope.

**Never render raw `error.message` / GraphQL `result.error.message` in the UI.** API and transport errors are English by convention; map
them through a bilingual helper (e.g. `uploadErrorMessage()` in `src/web/chat/fileUpload.ts` for uploads) or a generic `{ de, en }` fallback
such as “Speichern fehlgeschlagen.” / “Could not save.”

**PWA manifest** (`public/manifest.json`, when present) is a single static file with no locale switch — keep `name` / `short_name`
**brand-only** so install prompts are not locked to one language.

Voice and audience wording (plain language for end users vs operational admin labels, Du-form, device-not-session) live in
[styles/copy.md](./styles/copy.md). For bilingual **data** in Postgres, prefer paired `*De` / `*En` columns — see
[Bilingual columns](#bilingual-columns) above. Day-to-day locale strategy: [architecture/i18n.md](./architecture/i18n.md).

## Shared display formatting

Isomorphic date, currency, file-size, duration, participants, and euro-amount helpers live in `src/shared` (`formatDate`, `formatTime`,
`formatDateTime`, `formatDateRange`, `formatMonthYear`, `formatParticipants`, `formatCurrency`, `formatIsoDate`, `formatBytes`,
`formatDuration`, `formatHms`, `centsToEuros`, `eurosToCents`). Display helpers that need a locale require `{ locale: 'de' | 'en' }` and map
to `de-DE` / `en-US` via `languageTagFromLocale`. Date/time helpers accept an optional `timeZone`. In the UI pass the viewer zone from
`useTimeZone()`; in user-facing emails pass the recipient’s `Users.timeZone`; Slack ops may keep a fixed zone. Do **not** redefine local
`formatDate` / `formatTime` / `formatDateTime` / `formatParticipants` / `formatCurrency` / `formatBytes` helpers in routes or components —
import from `src/shared`. `formatCurrency` always shows **2 fraction digits** by default (e.g. `50,00 €` / `€50.00`); pass
`maximumFractionDigits: 0` only for whole-euro admin overview summaries. Relative time and calendar pickers still use `date-fns` +
`DATE_FNS_LOCALE` (see [i18n.md](./architecture/i18n.md)).

## Comments

Only add a comment if there is no other way to make the code self-explanatory. Reach for the alternatives first:

- A clearer name for the variable, function, or type
- A smaller, well-named helper function that captures the intent
- A more precise type that encodes the constraint
- Restructured control flow that removes the surprise

Comments are reserved for things the code itself cannot express: external context (a spec, a bug, a workaround), non-obvious **why**
decisions, or load-bearing invariants that aren't visible at the call site. The Arrange / Act / Assert markers in tests and the two-phase
markers in commands are intentional exceptions — they're structural, not explanatory.

If a comment paraphrases what the next line does, delete the comment and fix the line instead.

## Client bundle / code splitting

TanStack Start mounts the router code-splitter automatically (route `component` / `loader` boundaries). Still treat **static imports across
role shells** as a regression risk — a cook sidebar that imports `AccountPage` for a title string pulls the whole account module (and its
heavy deps) into every cook session.

Rules:

1. **Thin label modules for chrome titles.** Bilingual titles/descriptions shared by sidebars, breadcrumbs, and `seoMeta()` live in small
   `*Labels.ts` / `*ShellLabels.ts` files (e.g. `accountLabels.ts`, `adminShellLabels.ts`, `profileCookBookingRequestOfferLabels.ts`).
   Sidebars and breadcrumbs import **only** those — never a page module.
2. **Role shells are separate lazy chunks.** `ProfileLayout` dynamically imports cook vs customer shells so a customer never downloads cook
   nav/breadcrumb modules (and vice versa). Same for cook vs customer home on `ProfilePage`. **Eager `React.lazy` alone is not enough** —
   await the chunk from the route `loader` (`profileShellPreload` / `profileHomePreload`) so the download stays inside router `isLoading`
   and [NavigationProgress](./styles/navigation-progress.md) covers it. A post-loader `Suspense fallback={null}` is a blank white screen
   with no progress bar.
3. **Heavy optional UI is `React.lazy`.** Follow the Stripe pattern already documented in
   [`stripe-payment.md`](./architecture/stripe-payment.md): LiveKit call panel, image cropper, and admin assistant (Streamdown) load only
   when the user opens that surface. Those surfaces keep the previous page chrome visible, so a null Suspense fallback is fine.

After changing import graphs that cross admin / cook / customer / public, run a production build and confirm the entry / public /profile
chunks did not re-absorb the deferred packages (`livekit-client`, `react-easy-crop`, `@stripe/*`).

## UI Components

- **Pages vs routes.** Route files under `src/routes/` are thin wrappers: `createFileRoute`, `loader`, `head` / `seoMeta`, search
  validation, and a `component` that renders a page from `src/web/pages/`. Page UI, local state, and page-owned GraphQL documents live under
  `src/web/pages/` (mirror the route tree, e.g. `admin/AdminUsersPage.tsx`, `profile/ProfileCookMealsPage.tsx`). File / export / GraphQL
  operation stems follow [Page component naming](#page-component-naming).
- **Search before you create.** Before adding a new component (or hand-rolling markup that looks like one), search `src/web/components/`,
  `src/web/components/base/`, and `src/web/sections/` for an existing piece that already does the job — and check any relevant
  `docs/styles/*.md` catalog when the surface has one (e.g. chat). Prefer reuse or a small extension over a parallel one. A new file is
  justified only when nothing in that tree covers the interaction.
- Base components live in `src/web/components/base/` — these are Radix UI / shadcn primitives. Modify them sparingly.
- Application-specific components live directly in `src/web/components/`.
- Page sections (hero, feature blocks, etc.) live in `src/web/sections/` as `Section{Name}` (e.g. `SectionHero`). Compose them from pages;
  keep reusable chrome (nav, footer) in `src/web/components/`.
- Use the `cn()` utility from `src/web/utils/cn.ts` for conditional class merging.
- Prefer base primitives over native HTML form controls when a matching component exists (`Button`, `Input`, `Select`, `Combobox`,
  `Checkbox`, `Switch`, `Textarea`, `Dialog`, `AlertDialog`, `DatePicker`, …). Combobox is Base UI (`@base-ui/react`).
- **Children props.** Do not type `children: ReactNode` by hand. Named prop interfaces `extends PropsWithChildren` (from `react`); inline /
  type-alias props use `PropsWithChildren` or `PropsWithChildren<{ … }>`. Keep `ReactNode` only for non-`children` slots (`trailing`,
  `value`, `hint`, …).

### Forms (TanStack Form)

Multi-field edit / create forms use [`@tanstack/react-form`](https://tanstack.com/form) — not ad-hoc `useState` per field or a single
`useState` form blob.

- Create the form with `useForm({ defaultValues, onSubmit })`. Wire `<form onSubmit>` to `event.preventDefault()` +
  `void form.handleSubmit()`.
- Bind controls with `form.Field` (`field.state.value`, `field.handleChange`, `field.handleBlur`). Prefer base primitives inside the render
  prop.
- Read cross-field / submit UI state with `useSelector(form.store, selector)` (e.g. `isSubmitting`, values needed outside a `Field`).
- Resync from server/subscription updates with `form.reset(nextValues)`; patch a single value (uploads, combobox picks) with
  `form.setFieldValue`.
- Keep search filters, single toggles, and dialog one-liners on local state — TanStack Form is for structured field sets with Save / Submit.

Reference surfaces: `ProfileCookMealEditPage`, `ProfileCookMenuEditPage`, `ProfileCookChefProfileEditPage`,
`ProfileCustomerBookingRequestEditPage`.

### View-first entity details

Entity detail pages default to a **non-interactive view**. Technical edit forms (inputs, pinned Save footers, course editors) live behind an
explicit **Edit** step — prefer a sibling `/edit` route (`/profile/meals/$mealId/edit`, `/profile/chef-profile/edit`,
`/profile/travel/edit`, `/profile/booking-requests/$bookingRequestId/edit`) so Back / Cancel / breadcrumbs all exit edit cleanly. Publish,
delete, copy, and similar **actions** may stay on the view; only field editing moves to `/edit`.

Create flows that mint drafts (e.g. New meal / New menu) stay on the **list** after create — do not navigate into the editor.

**Excluded:** city, partner, and blog **page builders** (`ContentPageEditor` surfaces) stay editor-first — they are content composition
tools, not entity detail records.

### Profile pinned action footers

When a profile shell page needs actions always visible at the bottom of the inset pane (Save / Edit / Make offer / …), use
`ProfilePinnedFooterLayout` (`src/web/components/ProfilePinnedFooterLayout.tsx`). It fills the pane, scrolls the body, and pins the footer
row — that is the “sticky footer” pattern in product language, **not** CSS `position: sticky`. Pass `contentScroll={false}` when a child
(tab panel, chat transcript) owns scrolling — the default body scroller would otherwise keep an idle `scrollbar-gutter` strip on the right.
`contentClassName` (e.g. `grid content-start gap-6`) lands on an inner wrapper so the scrollport stays a block box — Chromium drops
`padding-bottom` when the overflow scroller is itself `display: grid` / `flex` (same class of bug as `workspace-inset-scroll`). For
equal-width paired actions on narrow panes, put `flex-1 md:flex-initial` on each footer button (footer row is `w-full`).

**Dirty Save gating (cook edit forms):** when the footer’s primary action is Save, show Save only while the form (or local edit state) is
dirty. When clean, replace Cancel+Save with a single back/view CTA (e.g. “Back to profile”). Applies to chef-profile, travel, meal, menu,
and offer price/menus edit under the cook shell.

Do **not** put `sticky bottom-0` action bars on pages that scroll with the cook/customer shell inset; short content leaves the bar mid-pane.
Customer booking-request edit keeps Cancel+Save always visible in the pinned footer (participants/restrictions live outside the TanStack
form dirty flag). Chat composers follow [`docs/styles/chat.md`](./styles/chat.md), not this wrapper. See also
[`docs/features/cook-shell.md`](./features/cook-shell.md) and [`docs/features/customer-shell.md`](./features/customer-shell.md).

**Nested scrollports clip paint outside the box.** `overflow-y-auto` / `overflow-hidden` (including the layout’s outer `overflow-hidden` and
offer-detail tab panels) clip `shadow-*`, `ring-*`, and focus rings at the edges. When a tab panel is the scroller under
`contentScroll={false}`, put the shell gutter on that panel (`px-4`) — not on the pinned-footer body — so the scrollbar sits on the pane
edge. A small extra inset (`px-1`) is only needed when a parent already supplies the main gutter. Chat composers keep their own padding so
the `InputGroup` focus ring is not clipped ([`docs/styles/chat.md`](./styles/chat.md)).

### Optional base primitives

These ship in `src/web/components/base/` for forks that need them. They are **not** workspace-mandated — use when the surface needs the
affordance; do not invent a parallel control when one of these already covers it:

| Primitive                                           | File                     | Use when                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Checkbox`                                          | `checkbox.tsx`           | Boolean form control (Radix)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `Combobox`                                          | `combobox.tsx`           | Searchable single-select (Base UI `@base-ui/react`). For server-driven lists (e.g. Places `locationSuggestions`), pass `filter={null}` so client substring filtering does not hide valid hits when typed order differs from `displayText`. Inside `Dialog`, the popup portals into the dialog host automatically (`PortalContainerProvider`) so Radix modal pointer-events do not block option clicks; pass `container` on `ComboboxContent` only to override. |
| `DateTimePicker`                                    | `date-time-picker.tsx`   | Date + time-of-day (requires bilingual `placeholder` / `timeAriaLabel`; composes `TimePicker`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `TimePicker`                                        | `time-picker.tsx`        | Time-of-day only: native `type="time"` below `md`, hour + minute `Select`s from `md` up (requires bilingual `hourAriaLabel` / `minuteAriaLabel`; optional `hourOptions` / `minuteOptions`, default 0–23 and `:00/:15/:30/:45`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `Marker` / `MarkerIcon` / `MarkerContent`           | `marker.tsx`             | Inline status, bordered rows, labeled separators                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `Tabs` / `TabsList` / `TabsTrigger` / `TabsContent` | `tabs.tsx`               | Sub-view / filter switchers (`TabsList variant="line"` for underlined top-of-page tabs; overflowing lists scroll **horizontally only** with edge fade, overflow-only chevrons, and vertical-wheel → horizontal remap on hover — never wrap `TabsList` in another scroller)                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `StatusIcon` / `StatusBadge` / `StatusAlert`        | `status-*.tsx`           | Incomplete / pending / success / error messaging — see [`docs/styles/status-messaging.md`](./styles/status-messaging.md)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `NotificationBadge`                                 | `notification-badge.tsx` | Unread count bubbles on cards and sidebar nav — see [`docs/styles/status-messaging.md`](./styles/status-messaging.md)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

App components for cook identity tags (not base primitives — live in `src/web/components/`):

| Component                            | File                  | Use when                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------ | --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `CookProfileTags` / `CookProfileTag` | `CookProfileTags.tsx` | Cuisine style + cooking philosophy pills on chef-profile read, public cook surfaces, offer cards, checkout. Muted fill (never `Badge secondary` on cards — secondary is white).                 |
| `PublicCookCard`                     | `PublicCookCard.tsx`  | Public cook discovery tile (square photo, name, city, `CookProfileTags`, compact rating when reviews exist; booking-card hover/pressed chrome) on `/chefs` and city / partner / occasion lists. |

Related hooks (also optional until a surface needs them): `useDebouncedValue`, `useVisualViewport`, `useHotkeys`, `useInView` under
`src/web/hooks/`. Scroll-reveal composition: `Reveal` in `src/web/components/Reveal.tsx` (see
[`docs/styles/motion.md`](./styles/motion.md)).

### Motion

Every animation must answer a question the user is already asking. Guardrails, anti-patterns, composer micro-states, and
`prefers-reduced-motion` live in [`docs/styles/motion.md`](./styles/motion.md). No motion library; reuse shared primitives (`Reveal` /
`useInView`) before inventing a one-off.

### Chat surfaces

Every chat surface follows the presentation rules in [`docs/styles/chat.md`](./styles/chat.md). Short version:

- Every composer wraps `MessageComposer` (`src/web/components/MessageComposer.tsx`). A raw `<textarea>` inside a chat surface is a
  review-time reject.
- Every transcript wraps `ChatTranscriptShell` (`src/web/components/base/chat-transcript-shell.tsx`). Pass `mode="assistant"` (default:
  last-anchor turn focus) or `mode="human"` (open/stick at absolute bottom for offer / support). Shared: `autoScroll`, 64 px edge, jump-to-
  latest. Do not hand-roll a second stick-to-bottom implementation per surface.
- Assistant text streams, unbubbled, with timestamp + copy underneath — always visible on touch. User rows may hover-reveal meta on
  fine-pointer devices only.

### Accessibility (landmarks & names)

- Every page-level content region is a single `<main id="main-content">`. Layout chrome that wraps the page (`SidebarInset` and similar)
  should be a `<div>` so pages do not nest landmarks. The root document mounts a bilingual skip link (`#main-content`) except on `/server/*`
  capture routes.
- **Outset rings / shadows need paint room.** Tailwind `ring-*` and card `shadow-*` paint outside the element box. Any ancestor with a
  non-`visible` overflow (including `overflow-y-auto`, which also clips the cross axis) will shear them at the scrollport edge. The profile
  cook/customer shell puts default scroll on the padded content pane so page `<main>`s stay unclipped; nested scroll containers (chat rows,
  tab panes, dialogs) must inset themselves — see `MessageScrollerItem`’s `p-1` pattern and [motion.md](./styles/motion.md).
- Icon-only controls need an accessible name (`aria-label` / `sr-only`). Hover-reveal row actions use `pointer-fine:opacity-0` so touch
  users still see them, plus `focus-within:opacity-100` for keyboard.

## GraphQL

- The schema is defined SDL-first in `src/server/graphql/schema.graphqls`.
- After any schema change, run `npm run graphql:generate` to regenerate types.
- Server-side generated types use the `GqlS` prefix; client-side types use `GqlC`.
- All resolvers are wired in `src/server/graphql/resolversCreate.ts` — this is the only file that should import from commands/, queries/,
  and guards/. **Resolvers stay thin:** one call to a command or query (plus a guard / `assertLegalAcceptanceCurrent` when the field is a
  write namespace child). No DB access, no mapping, no third-party SDK calls in the resolver body.
- **Commands and queries take generated `GqlS…Args` (or the parent object for field resolvers) as their GraphQL input** — do not unpack
  `args.criterion` / `args.mealId` in the resolver. Unpack inside the command/query if needed.
- **Commands and queries must not import each other** (CQRS). Enforced by ESLint `no-restricted-imports` on `src/server/commands/**` and
  `src/server/queries/**`. If a command needs a read, inline the select or extract a helper outside `queries/`.
- Union and interface `__resolveType` declarations go in `src/server/graphql/extensions.ts` via module augmentation.
- Client-side `.graphql` operation files go alongside the page or component that uses them: `src/web/pages/**/*.graphql`,
  `src/web/components/**/*.graphql`, or `src/web/chat/**/*.graphql`. Route files under `src/routes/` stay thin wrappers (loader / `head` /
  search) and should not own operation documents.
- Membership probes use real ids (`Admin.adminId`, `Cook.cookId`), not artificial `ok` booleans. Nullable `User.admin` / `User.cook` remain
  the presence check; clients select `adminId` / `cookId` when they need a selection set. Mutation write namespaces stamp actor ids only via
  `extensions.ts` (`GqlSUserMutation.userId`, `GqlSCookMutation.cookId`, `GqlSAdminMutation.adminId`) — never on the SDL.

## Commands (Database Writes)

Commands in `src/server/commands/` follow a two-phase structure: **payload construction**, then **transactional execution**.

### Structure

```typescript
export async function orderCreate(db: Database, input: OrderInput): Promise<GqlSOrder> {
  // Phase 1 — Payload construction (pure, no DB calls)
  const orderInsert: OrderCreate = {
    orderId: idCreate(),
    customerId: input.customerId,
    status: 'pending',
  };

  const orderItemInserts: OrderItemCreate[] = input.items.map((item) => ({
    orderItemId: idCreate(),
    orderId: orderInsert.orderId,
    productId: item.productId,
    quantity: item.quantity,
  }));

  // Phase 2 — Transactional execution (side-effectful)
  try {
    const order = await db.transaction(async (transaction) => {
      const [created] = await transaction.insert(orders).values(orderInsert).returning();
      await transaction.insert(orderItems).values(orderItemInserts);
      return created!;
    });

    return toGqlOrder(order);
  } catch (error) {
    console.error(error);
    throw error;
  }
}
```

### Rules

1. **Phase 1 — Payload construction** comes first. Build all insert/update objects before touching the database. This phase is pure: no DB
   calls, no side effects. If it fails (e.g. a Zod parse), no connection or transaction is ever opened.
2. **Phase 2 — Transactional execution** wraps all DB calls in `db.transaction(async (transaction) => { ... })`. Use `transaction` (not
   `db`) for every query inside the transaction. Wrap in try-catch, log the error, and re-throw.
3. **Single-write commands** do not need a transaction — individual statements are already atomic in PostgreSQL. Use the two-phase structure
   (payload, then single DB call in try-catch) but skip `db.transaction()`.
4. **The `DatabaseTransaction` type** is exported from `src/server/db/index.ts`. Use it when passing a transaction handle to helper
   functions.

## Package Manager

npm only. The `engines` field in `package.json` enforces this — pnpm and yarn are blocked.

## SEO

Every public page route MUST set `head: ({ params }) => seoMeta({ ... })` using the helper at `src/web/seo/seoMeta.ts`. Pages that are
logged-in, transactional, or otherwise non-indexable pass `noindex: true`. Indexable public pages are also added to `SITEMAP_PATHS` in
`src/web/seo/sitemapRoutes.ts` so they appear in `/sitemap-pages.xml` (discovered via the `/sitemap.xml` index).

See [architecture/discovery-seo.md](./architecture/discovery-seo.md) for the full rationale, the canonical/hreflang strategy, and a
copy-paste template for new pages.

## Environment Variables

Never read `process.env` directly. The only sanctioned reader is `src/server/env/environmentVariablesCreate.ts`; everything else (including
`drizzle.config.ts` and test utilities) calls `environmentVariablesCreate()` to get a typed, validated object. This is enforced by an ESLint
`no-restricted-syntax` rule — any new `process.env` reference will fail lint. See
[docs/architecture/environment.md](./architecture/environment.md) for the rationale.

## Testing

### Runner

Unit and integration tests use [Vitest](https://vitest.dev/). Run them with:

```bash
npm test
```

Multi-party UI journeys use Playwright (`@playwright/test`). Run them with:

```bash
npm run test:e2e
# interactive UI mode:
npm run test:e2e:ui
```

See [architecture/e2e.md](./architecture/e2e.md) for the actor/world model, cookie auth, and how e2e differs from production browser
capture. Keep authorization matrices and radius filters in Vitest; use e2e for thin multi-party UI proofs.

### Configuration — two projects

Vitest config lives in **`vitest.config.ts`**, separate from `vite.config.ts`. The dev/build config loads the full TanStack Start + Nitro +
React plugin stack, which Vitest 4 + Vite 8's module runner cannot evaluate against React's CJS entry — keeping it loaded during tests
produces a `ReferenceError: module is not defined` at startup.

`vitest.config.ts` defines two projects with disjoint plugin sets:

| Project  | Environment | Plugins                  | Includes                                                      |
| -------- | ----------- | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `server` | `node`      | none                     | `src/server/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}`                               |
| `web`    | `jsdom`     | `@vitejs/plugin-react()` | `src/web/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}`, `src/routes/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}` |

Run a single project with `npm test -- --project=web` (or `--project=server`).

### Setup files

- `src/server/test/vitestSetup.ts` runs in **both** projects. It globally spies on `console.log/error/warn/info/debug` with a no-op so the
  logger's stdout echo doesn't pollute reporter output, and so any test can assert on calls via
  `expect(console.error).toHaveBeenCalledWith(...)` without per-file `vi.spyOn` boilerplate.
- `src/web/test/vitestSetup.ts` runs only in the `web` project. It calls `cleanup()` from `@testing-library/react` after each test so
  `document.body` is reset between renders.

`clearMocks: true` is set at the top level so it applies to both projects — `vi.fn()` call history resets between tests automatically.

### Structure — Arrange / Act / Assert

Every test case follows the **Arrange → Act → Assert** pattern with explicit comments:

```typescript
it('creates a new session when no existing session ID is provided', async () => {
  // Arrange
  const input = buildInput();

  // Act
  const result = await sessionUpsert(testDb, testLog, input);

  // Assert
  expect(result.sessionId).toBeDefined();
});
```

Use `// Arrange — nothing` when the test needs no setup.

### Unit tests

Place test files next to the module they test with a `.test.ts` (or `.test.tsx` for React) suffix:

```
src/server/utils/sessionUtils.ts
src/server/utils/sessionUtils.test.ts

src/web/components/base/button.tsx
src/web/components/base/button.test.tsx
```

Server unit tests cover pure or near-pure functions and should not touch the database. Web unit tests use `@testing-library/react`
(`render`, `screen`) — see `src/web/components/base/button.test.tsx` for the canonical shape.

### Integration tests (database)

Tests that hit the database use the shared test utilities in `src/server/test/commandTestUtils.ts`:

| Export                    | Purpose                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `testDb`                  | Drizzle client connected to the test DB                                                                                        |
| `testLog`                 | Logger wired to the test DB                                                                                                    |
| `commandSetup()`          | Persists a fresh session row + a fresh `ServerRuntime` stub; returns `{ serverRuntime, requestingSession }`                    |
| `commandSetup.withUser()` | Same, plus a seeded `users` row (far-future legal acceptance by default); returns `{ serverRuntime, requestingSession, user }` |
| `findLogsForSession`      | Drains the async logger queue then returns the `Logs` rows for a `sessionId`                                                   |

**Always use a real database** — never mock Drizzle or the database layer. Each `commandSetup()` call mints fresh ids (`idCreate()`), so
tests do not collide and there is no need for cleanup hooks between them. `vitest.config.ts` sets `clearMocks: true`, which resets `vi.fn()`
call history between tests, so individual tests do not need a `beforeEach(vi.clearAllMocks)` of their own.

### Command tests — required coverage

Every command under `src/server/commands/` must have colocated tests (`.test.ts`, or a small combined file when several tightly related
commands share setup — e.g. `authEmailOtp.test.ts`, `cookCallAvailability.test.ts`) that cover **every logical path** and assert **every
side effect**:

| Side effect                    | How to assert                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| DB insert / update / delete    | `testDb.select()…` after the act (and before, when proving a no-op / rejection left state unchanged) |
| `publish.*`                    | `toHaveBeenCalledWith(...)` / `not.toHaveBeenCalled()` on the stub from `commandSetup`               |
| `email.send`                   | `toHaveBeenCalled…` on `serverRuntime.email.send`                                                    |
| `jobs.enqueue` / `jobs.cancel` | `toHaveBeenCalledWith(definition, data, …)` / `not.toHaveBeenCalled()` on `serverRuntime.jobs.*`     |
| Stripe / Places / browser      | `toHaveBeenCalled…` on the matching `serverRuntime.*` stub                                           |
| `log.error` on failure         | `findLogsForSession(sessionId)` after the throw (drains the async logger queue)                      |

**Jobs are a dispatch side effect only in command tests.** Assert that the correct definition + payload (and cancel, when applicable) were
requested — do **not** exercise the handler body from the command suite. Handler behavior lives in colocated job handler tests (see
[Job handler tests](#job-handler-tests) below). `commandSetup` stubs `jobs.enqueue` as a resolved `vi.fn()`, so commands never run pg-boss
or the handler.

Skip only paths that are unreachable without mocking the database itself. Prefer real DB + stubbed runtime I/O over mocking Drizzle.

The canonical command test (see `src/server/commands/userUpdate.test.ts`) follows this shape — no `beforeAll`, no `beforeEach`, no shared
runtime; each `it` arranges what it needs:

```typescript
describe('userUpdate', () => {
  it('updates the row and publishes a userUpdates event on success', async () => {
    // Arrange
    const { serverRuntime, requestingSession, user } = await commandSetup.withUser({ firstName: 'original', lastName: 'User' });

    // Act
    const result = await userUpdate(
      { userId: user.userId } as GqlSUserMutation,
      { user: { firstName: 'renamed' } },
      requestingSession,
      serverRuntime,
    );

    // Assert
    expect(result).toEqual({ success: true });
    expect(serverRuntime.publish.userUpdates).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ userId: user.userId });
  });
});
```

Environment variables for integration tests come from the shell environment. Unit tests must not depend on `.env` files — pass any required
config explicitly (e.g. inject a source object into `environmentVariablesCreate`).

### Query tests — required coverage

Every query under `src/server/queries/` must have colocated tests (`.test.ts`, or a small combined file when several tightly related queries
share setup — e.g. `adminSessionCounts.test.ts` also covering `adminSessionCreationsFindMany`) that hit the **real database** via
`commandSetup` / `testDb`. Never mock Drizzle. Follow Arrange → Act → Assert with explicit comments; isolate exact counts with unique tokens
/ nanoIds so parallel workers sharing the test DB do not collide.

Required cases by query kind:

| Kind                         | Required cases                                                         |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| FindOne                      | mapped hit; unknown id → `null` (or documented throw)                  |
| FindMany (criterion)         | order; each filter axis; `skip`/`take`; empty enum filter → `[]`       |
| Count                        | same filters as sibling FindMany; empty enum filter → `0`              |
| Counts / time buckets        | shape + lower bounds / ascending zero-filled series                    |
| Ownership / parent resolvers | owner session success; foreign session → `null` / `[]`                 |
| Public published             | published included; unpublished excluded; path miss → `null`           |
| Soft-delete / offer menus    | deleted / offer menus excluded                                         |
| Places                       | stub `serverRuntime.places.locationSuggestions` via `vi.mocked`        |
| Booking                      | happy path + ownership / key filters (seed from command-test patterns) |

The canonical query test (see `src/server/queries/adminUserFindOne.test.ts` / `adminUserFindMany.test.ts`) follows the same shape as command
tests — no `beforeAll`, no `beforeEach`, no shared runtime; each `it` arranges what it needs.

### Job handler tests

Every job under `src/server/jobs/handlers/` must have a colocated `.test.ts` that calls `definition.handler({ data, serverRuntime })` (or an
exported run helper when the definition only wraps one). Same integration rules as commands: real DB via `commandSetup` / `testDb`, stub
runtime I/O (`email`, `stripe`, `slack`, `jobs`, …). Mock sibling commands / send helpers with `vi.mock` when the handler only orchestrates
them.

Cover every logical path the handler owns: happy side effects, defensive no-ops (missing row, already-terminal status, unread cleared), and
failure paths that update domain state or rethrow. Do **not** rely on command tests to cover handler logic — those only assert enqueue /
cancel.

Canonical examples: `giftCardPreparedExpire.test.ts`, `userKlaviyoProfileSync.test.ts`, `bookingRequestOfferPullPayment.test.ts`.

## Commit Messages

Commits follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) and are linted by [commitlint](https://commitlint.js.org/) using
`@commitlint/config-conventional` (see `commitlint.config.ts`).

```
<type>(<optional scope>): <subject>
```

Common types: `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `refactor`, `test`, `chore`, `perf`, `build`, `ci`, `style`, `revert`.

```bash
# Good
feat(chat): stream agent responses over SSE
fix: guard against missing session cookie

# Bad — will fail commitlint
updated stuff
WIP
```

Enforcement happens in two places:

- A Husky `commit-msg` hook (`.husky/commit-msg`) runs `commitlint --edit $1` locally on every commit. `npm run prepare` (executed
  automatically on `npm install`) installs the hook.
- `npm run commitlint:check` lints the most recent commit and is part of `npm run check`. It uses `HEAD~1..HEAD` when a parent exists,
  otherwise the empty tree so the initial commit is included.

## Deprecated APIs

Do not call APIs marked `@deprecated` in their type definitions (Zod string-format methods like `z.string().email()`, AI SDK
`result.response` / `fullStream`, React `MutableRefObject` / `FormEvent`, etc.). Prefer the replacement named in the deprecation message
(e.g. `z.email()`, `result.finalStep.response`, `result.stream`, `RefObject`, `SubmitEvent`).

This is enforced by ESLint `@typescript-eslint/no-deprecated` on type-aware lint paths (`src/server/**`, `src/shared/**`) — `tsc` does not
fail on deprecations on its own. `npm run lint:check` (and therefore `npm run check`) will reject new usages there. Web/routes and other
bulk paths use `typescript-eslint`’s `disableTypeChecked` so ESLint does not load their TypeScript program (see `eslint.config.js`).

## Import Ordering

Import order is enforced by ESLint (`import/order` + `sort-imports` in `eslint.config.js`) and autofixed by `npm run lint` / editor
`source.fixAll.eslint` on save. Do not hand-sort imports — let the fixer own it.

Rules:

1. Groups, in order: builtin → external → internal → parent → sibling → index
2. Alphabetize by module path within each group (case-insensitive)
3. Named members inside `{ … }` are alphabetized (`sort-imports`)
4. `import type` stays with its module path (not a separate trailing type-only group) — matches
   `import/consistent-type-specifier-style: prefer-top-level` from the TanStack config

```ts
import { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { eq } from 'drizzle-orm';
import { ToolLoopAgent } from 'ai';
import type { ServerRuntime } from '../domain/ServerRuntime';
import { userAssistantChatFindOne } from '../queries/userAssistantChatFindOne';
import { toolProjectsList } from './toolProjectsList';
```

## Tailwind Canonical Classes

Prefer Tailwind’s canonical class form. ESLint enforces this via `better-tailwindcss/enforce-canonical-classes` (same suggestions as the
IntelliSense `suggestCanonicalClasses` diagnostic). Companion rule `better-tailwindcss/no-unnecessary-whitespace` keeps class strings tidy
after collapses.

Examples:

| Prefer            | Over                      |
| ----------------- | ------------------------- |
| `text-sm/relaxed` | `text-sm leading-relaxed` |
| `bg-linear-to-tr` | `bg-gradient-to-tr`       |
| `p-5`             | `px-5 py-5`               |
| `md:p-6`          | `md:px-6 md:py-6`         |

Fix with `npm run lint`. The editor’s IntelliSense copy of this lint is turned off in `.vscode/settings.json`
(`tailwindCSS.lint.suggestCanonicalClasses: ignore`) so you only see ESLint.

## Storybook

Component stories live next to the component as `*.stories.tsx` (discovered by `.storybook/main.ts`). Deploy / Coolify stays in
[infrastructure.md](./infrastructure.md#storybook--email-preview-coolify).

### Start here

1. **`Foundations/Mood Board`** — product style and mood in one scroll (tokens, status vs brand, card family, chat)
2. **`Foundations/Tokens`** — surface swatches, type scale, status / booking pill reference
3. **`Perspectives/*`** — role parity (Customer · Cook · Admin) and surface collages (discovery, booking desk)
4. Atomic groups (`Base`, `Chat`, `Booking`, …) — variant depth for a single component

Composition stories only import existing components and fixtures. They do not introduce new product UI.

### Titles (hybrid taxonomy)

| Sidebar group  | Use for                                                                                        |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Foundations`  | Mood board and token / type reference (composition-only; no new product components)            |
| `Base`         | Radix / shadcn primitives under `src/web/components/base/`                                     |
| `Chat`         | Transcript atoms, composer, message variants, chat surfaces                                    |
| `Booking`      | Request / offer / call / cost cards and banners                                                |
| `Discovery`    | Public cook / meal / menu discovery tiles                                                      |
| `Support`      | Support request list chrome                                                                    |
| `Perspectives` | Side-by-side role galleries and surface collages (composition-only; no new product components) |

Titles match `Base/Button` style: `Foundations/Mood Board`, `Chat/Composer`, `Booking/Customer Offer Card`, `Perspectives/Offer Cards`.

### Authoring

- Prefer presentational props and stub callbacks (`fn()` / async no-ops). Do not call production GraphQL from stories.
- Shared fixtures live in [`src/web/storybook/fixtures/`](../src/web/storybook/fixtures/) (`people`, `booking`, `chat`, `calls`).
- Gallery chrome for compositions: [`src/web/storybook/gallery.tsx`](../src/web/storybook/gallery.tsx) (`WarmPage`, `GallerySection`,
  `RoleColumn`, `SurfaceColumn`). Prefer `WarmPage` (`bg-background`) so white / secondary surfaces lift off the warm canvas.
- Global preview wraps locale toolbar (DE / EN), `TimeZoneProvider` (`Europe/Berlin`), `TooltipProvider`, stub urql, and a memory router
  with `/$locale` so `useLocale` works.
- Reusable decorators: [`.storybook/decorators.tsx`](../.storybook/decorators.tsx) (`cardCanvasDecorator`, `chatViewportDecorator`,
  `perspectivesCanvasDecorator`, `withFeatureToggles`). Locale / timezone come from the global preview.
- Use `interactive={false}` on cards that support it when the story is about chrome / status, not navigation.
- Defer LiveKit call panels, mutation-bound schedule tabs, and assistant `ChatMessagePartsView` until they have presentational extracts.

Local: `npm run storybook` (port 6006), `npm run storybook:build`.

## Quality Checks

Run all checks before pushing:

```bash
npm run check
```

This runs: format check, type check, lint, spell check, unused export detection (knip), and commitlint on the last commit. Type check runs
before lint so type errors fail fast instead of after a long ESLint pass.

## Browser Capture (Playwright)

The template ships a server-side image-rendering pipeline. To use it:

- **Never `import 'playwright'` directly.** Capture is exposed on the runtime as `serverRuntime.browser.capture(options)`. Tests inject a
  stub.
- **Render targets live under `/server/*`** (e.g. `src/routes/server.reports.$reportId.tsx`). They authenticate with a one-shot HMAC token
  from `src/server/utils/serverToken.ts`, not the session cookie. `__root` should omit nav-progress / toaster / floating chrome on these
  paths and force a white / neutral body so PDF pages don't pick up site chrome or themed `--background`.
- **The signing secret is `SERVER_TOKEN_SECRET`** (capability-specific — only required by features that actually call `browserCapture`). Set
  it in `.env.local` and in your Coolify environment.
- **Do not edit `vite.config.ts`'s Playwright externals or the runtime stage of `Dockerfile`** without reading
  [architecture/browser-capture.md](./architecture/browser-capture.md) — `playwright` must stay external on both, and the runtime image must
  keep installing Chromium.

## Jobs (Background Processing)

- Job handler files live in `src/server/jobs/handlers/` and follow entity-action naming: `{entityAction}.ts` (e.g.,
  `bookingRequestSlackDigest.ts`, `giftCardPreparedExpire.ts`)
- Each handler file exports a single `JobDefinition` (either `RecurringJobDefinition` or `QueuedJobDefinition`)
- All jobs are registered in `src/server/jobs/jobDefinitions.ts` — this is the single wiring point (analogous to `resolversCreate.ts` for
  GraphQL)
- Enqueue queued jobs via `serverRuntime.jobs.enqueue(definition, data, options)` — the definition provides type safety
- Re-export handler definitions from `src/server/jobs/index.ts` for ergonomic imports
- pg-boss manages its own `pgboss` schema in PostgreSQL — do not create Drizzle migrations for it
- Colocate handler tests as `{entityAction}.test.ts` — see [Job handler tests](#job-handler-tests). Callers assert enqueue only.
